Calories in Spanish food, per serving and per 100 g

How many calories are in Spanish food? A table of what people really eat in Spain: the serving as it is served, its calories, and per 100 g so you can compare. Each dish has its own page with the protein, carbs and fat, what a serving weighs and how it compares.

Quick answer: a Spanish dish has between 90 and 594 kcal per serving: from Gazpacho (cold tomato soup) (90 kcal, 250 g) to Cocido madrileño (Madrid chickpea stew) (594 kcal, 400 g). The middle dish of the 25 in this table is Spanish meatballs in sauce (albóndigas en salsa), with 394 kcal. Figures from the Fotocal database, built from USDA and CIQUAL.

Serving: the one the Fotocal app uses for each dish, in grams as served. Figures come from public databases (USDA FoodData Central and CIQUAL 2025) added up ingredient by ingredient; each page says exactly which rows.

How to read the table

The serving column is the one that matters day to day: it is what you log if you eat the dish. Per 100 g is for comparing dishes and for working out a different amount: weigh what you have, multiply by the figure and divide by 100.

The whole app database, 218 foods and dishes, is in the full calorie table. To work out how much you should eat, try the eight calculators, starting with daily calories.
